a tubular acoustic device inserted in the exhaust system that is designed to reduce noise

wiktionary.gloss: An attachment to a gun that reduces the sound it emits.
The muffler of an internal combustion engine.
Any of various devices to silence the humming noise of telegraph wires.
Something that prevents or greatly reduces gene expression.

senses.definition: sloping in one direction rather than straight or level

examples.en: The house has a slanted wooden roof.
examples.vi: Ngôi nhà có một mái gỗ dốc nghiêng.

examples.en: Her handwriting was slanted to the right.
examples.vi: Chữ viết tay của cô ấy nghiêng về phía bên phải.

senses.definition: showing an unfair preference for one opinion or side

examples.en: The article gave a slanted view of the election.
examples.vi: Bài báo đưa ra một cái nhìn thiên kiến về cuộc bầu cử.

thesaurus.definition: having an oblique or slanted direction
favoring one person or side over another

vi_block: Thiên kiến; có thái độ có thành kiến, cách nhìn có thành kiến, quan điểm có thành kiến.

wiktionary.gloss: Placed at an angle, on a slant.

examples: The news report was slanted in favor of the nationalists.
wiktionary.gloss: Biased.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from translingual Sphagnum, which is from Ancient Greek σφάγνος (sphágnos).

thesaurus.definition: any of various pale or ashy mosses of the genus Sphagnum whose decomposed remains form peat

examples: [T]he ground up here is waterlogged and riddled with potholes, holes beneath the spongy coral fern, hidden holes throughout the sphagnum.
wiktionary.gloss: Any of various widely distributed mosses, of genus Sphagnum, which slowly decompose to form peat.

blocks.etymology: From Afrikaans steenbok, from Dutch steenbok.

thesaurus.definition: small plains antelope of southeastern Africa

wiktionary.gloss: A common small antelope of southern and eastern Africa, Raphicerus campestris.

blocks.etymology: From Latin sylvāticus. See sylvan. Doublet of savage.
vi_block: Tác động đến dã thú trong rừng.

wiktionary.gloss: Of or pertaining to woods or woodland organisms; sylvan
Of or pertaining to wild rather than domestic animals
Of or pertaining to diseases or parasites borne or transmitted by sylvatic organisms

blocks.etymology: From Latin sylvāticus. See sylvan. Doublet of savage.

wiktionary.gloss: A wild animal

blocks.etymology: From a childish pronunciation of sweet. The Oxford English Dictionary records the first use in 1905 in Punch.

thesaurus.definition: affectedly dainty or refined

vi_block: sướt mướt (hấp dẫn với những người có thị hiếu đa cảm hoặc thấp kém).

examples: Those Beatrix Potter animals are a little twee for my taste.
wiktionary.gloss: Overly quaint, dainty, cute or nice.

blocks.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *n̥- From un- + befriended.

wiktionary.gloss: Not befriended; lacking friends.

blocks.etymology: From underachieve + -er or under- + achiever.

thesaurus.definition: a student who does not perform as well as expected or as well as the IQ indicates

vi_block: Người làm kém, người làm không được tốt như mong đợi (nhất là về học tập).

wiktionary.gloss: One who underachieves, i.e. performs less well than expected.

blocks.etymology: From unyielding + -ly.

wiktionary.gloss: In an unyielding way.

blocks.etymology: Partly from German, see wels.
